body:
Shopping for vape hardware means meeting a lot of unfamiliar words: drip tip, 510 connector, atomizer, pod, airflow ring. This labeled guide walks through every part you are likely to see on a device or a product page, what it does, how it differs between device types, which parts wear out, which parts are interchangeable and how to match replacements to your exact device. It is written for beginners aged 21 and over, with plain explanations and practical tips. Nicotine is addictive.

## How to use this guide
Read it once to learn the vocabulary, then come back to it when you compare products. Each section names a part, says what it does and notes what to look for when you buy. If a word on a product page is not here, check our [vape glossary of terms](/blog/vape-glossary-terms-a-to-z/).

## Mouthpiece (drip tip)
The part you draw from. On tanks, mouthpieces are often interchangeable, and they come in different widths and materials, such as plastic, resin or metal. A narrow mouthpiece suits a tight, cigarette-style draw, and a wide one suits an open draw. On disposables and many pods, the mouthpiece is fixed. If you share devices, a replaceable mouthpiece is easier to keep clean. Keep it dry and wipe it regularly.

## Tank or pod
Holds the e-liquid. Tanks are larger and refilled through a fill port, which is usually a sliding or screw-off cover. Pods are compact cartridges that snap into the battery, either pre-filled or refillable. Pre-filled pods are replaced when empty, and refillable pods are topped up. See [what a pod vape is](/blog/what-is-a-pod-vape-and-how-to-choose/). Capacity is listed in milliliters, and a larger capacity means fewer refills but a bulkier device.

### Fill port and seal
The fill port is where you add liquid. A good seal keeps it from leaking, so check that the cover is fully closed. Overfilling is a common cause of leaks, and our guide to [filling a pod without leaks](/blog/how-to-fill-a-pod-without-leaks/) explains how to avoid it.

## Coil
The heating element, usually mesh or wire. It heats the liquid and wears out over time, so it needs replacing. In many pods, the coil is built into the pod. In tanks, it is a separate part that screws in. Coils have a resistance, measured in ohms, and a recommended power range. Learn [mesh versus standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/) and [what a mesh coil is](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).

## Wick
Cotton or another absorbent material inside the coil that carries liquid to the heating surface. You do not see it, but its condition decides how well the device works. A wick that is dry or burnt gives a harsh taste, and a wick that is flooded gives gurgling and leaks. Priming a new coil lets the wick soak properly. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

## Battery
Powers the heater. Capacity is measured in mAh, and in many devices the battery is built in and recharged through a port. In box mods, it may be one or two removable cells. Larger capacity usually means longer life between charges, but power use also matters. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/) and [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Airflow control
A ring or slider that adjusts air intake. Open airflow gives a looser, cooler draw and more vapor. Tight airflow gives a restricted draw that suits mouth-to-lung inhaling. Not every device has it. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## 510 connector
A standard threaded connection, named for its thread pattern, that lets many tanks fit many mods. It is the reason you can pair a tank from one brand with a mod from another. Pods and disposables do not use it. If you buy a tank for a mod, check that both use a 510 thread, and that the tank's recommended power matches the mod.

## Charging port
Modern devices use USB-C. Older devices use micro-USB or proprietary connectors. USB-C is reversible and common, so cables are easy to find. A charging port can collect lint and residue, so keep it clean and dry. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/).

## Fire button and sensor
Devices fire on inhale (auto-draw) or when you press a button. The sensor that detects your draw is a small component near the airflow path. If it gets blocked by liquid, the device may stop firing. See [auto-draw vs button-fire](/blog/auto-draw-vs-button-fire-vapes/).

## Display and indicator lights
Some devices have a screen that shows battery, power or liquid levels, and others have a light that changes color or blinks to signal status. See [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/) and [screen vs no-screen disposables](/blog/screen-vs-no-screen-disposable-vapes/).

## Other parts you may see
- **O-rings and seals:** rubber rings that keep the tank sealed.
- **Base and deck:** the bottom of a tank, where the coil sits.
- **Glass or tube:** the clear section of a tank that shows the liquid level.
- **Chimney or center tube:** the channel that carries vapor to the mouthpiece.
- **Lanyard or case:** accessories for carrying.

## Which parts wear out
- **Coils and pods:** wear first, and are replaced regularly.
- **O-rings:** harden over time and may need replacing if a tank leaks.
- **Mouthpieces:** can crack or stain.
- **Batteries:** lose capacity after many cycles.

See [how to pick replacement coils and pods](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/).

## Matching replacements to your device
Replacement parts must match your exact device. Check the product name and model, the thread type for tanks, the coil resistance and the recommended power. Pods and coils are not interchangeable between brands or often between models. If you are unsure, ask us with your device name. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Which part should I replace first when flavor fades?
The coil or pod. It is the most common cause, and replacing it is the simplest fix.

### Can I use a different brand's pod?
Usually not. Pods are designed for a specific device, and a mismatch can leak or not fit.

### What does 510 mean?
It is the name of a standard thread size that lets tanks and mods from different makers connect.

### How do I clean the parts?
Wipe the outside with a dry cloth. Rinse refillable tanks with warm water, dry them fully and reassemble. Do not wet the battery or the electronics. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

## Shopping
Match replacement parts to your exact device. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Putting the parts together: three example devices
### A disposable
A disposable has a body, a built-in battery, a pre-filled liquid reservoir, a coil with a wick, an airflow sensor, a mouthpiece and often a USB-C port. You cannot separate the parts, and you do not need to. The parts you can affect are the charging and the way you use it. When the liquid or the battery is finished, you replace the whole thing.

### A pod system
A pod system has a battery section with a sensor and a port, and a pod that clicks into it. The pod contains the liquid, the wick and often the coil. When the pod is empty or the coil wears out, you replace the pod. The battery stays. If the pod is refillable, you can add liquid through a fill port until the coil wears out.

### A tank and mod
A tank and mod has a mod with one or two batteries, a screen and buttons, and a tank that screws onto the 510 connector. The tank has a mouthpiece, a glass section, a fill port, an airflow ring and a replaceable coil. You can change the coil, the mouthpiece, the glass and sometimes the airflow. This type has the most parts, and the most to look after.

## A quick buying checklist by part
- **Mouthpiece:** comfortable, and easy to keep clean.
- **Tank or pod:** a capacity that suits your use, and a seal that does not leak.
- **Coil:** the right resistance and type for your style, and replacements that are easy to find.
- **Battery:** a capacity and charging port that suit you, with a reputable maker.
- **Airflow:** adjustable if you want to tune the draw.
- **Connector:** standard if you want to mix and match.
- **Display:** useful if you want to see battery and power at a glance.

## Cleaning and care by part
Wipe mouthpieces regularly. Rinse refillable tanks and glass sections with warm water, and let them dry fully before use. Never wet the battery or the electronics. Check O-rings for wear, and replace them if they harden or crack. Replace coils and pods when flavor fades. Check the charging port for lint, and clear it gently with a dry tool if needed. A few minutes of care keeps parts working for longer.

## Where parts come from
Parts are made by the device maker or by third parties. Original parts fit best and follow the maker's specifications. Third-party parts can be a good value but vary in quality, so choose carefully. For sealed devices, there are no user-serviceable parts, and the whole device is replaced.

### Frequently asked questions about parts
**Can I swap the mouthpiece on a pod?** Usually not, because it is built into the pod. On a tank, many mouthpieces can be swapped if they use the same standard fitting.

**Why does my tank leak around the base?** Often an O-ring has worn, the coil is loose or the tank is overfilled. Check each in turn.
